A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FairNVT, with matching authors, framework and benchmark tasks despite the revised title. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original FairNVT experiments on CelebA, UTKFace and BIOS, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations, attacker evaluations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark and ablation results, including additional Pareto analyses, representation-specific attacks, batch-size experiments and inference-variability measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the orthogonality objective from squared cosine similarity alone to cosine similarity plus HSIC between task embeddings and sensitive labels. This adds a direct statistical-dependence penalty to the task branch, materially changing its optimization. The dual adapters, Gaussian perturbation, concatenation and primary inference procedure remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same CelebA attribute pairs, UTKFace gender/age classification and BIOS profession/gender task, including the appendix benchmarks and gender-swapped biographies. New experiments vary training, representations and attacker procedures within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds FairNet to the image comparisons in Table 1 and appendix Table 13. The existing quantitative image and text comparators remain. FairVPT is removed from the saliency comparisons in v2 Figures 3 and 5, although it remains in the numerical comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation across hyperparameter configurations, attacks on individual branches and averaged noisy embeddings, batch-size variation, and fixed-checkpoint inference repeats. Appendix C changes learning-rate search spacing from half-orders to full orders of magnitude, clipping thresholds from {1,10,100} to {1,10}, and loss weights from {0,0.1,0.3,0.5,1,3} to {0.1,0.3,0.5,1}. These are reported protocol changes; they do not establish which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds Pareto analyses, staged adapter/loss ablations, branch-specific leakage and repeated-observation attacks, batch-size sensitivity, and isolated inference variability. Earlier noise-strength and deeper-attacker analyses are retained with revisions. The pure-noise-plus-task control and majority-vote inference study are removed, while the Big Nose/Age factorial ablation is replaced by staged comparisons.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run means and standard deviations for the main benchmarks. V2 adds three inference-only repetitions at a fixed checkpoint and explains the sources of main-result variability. It also explicitly labels several appendix ablations as single-run, same-seed results and removes uncertainty estimates from retained noise-strength, classifier-input and deeper-attacker comparisons.

E6.justification: Numerous Table 1 values and rankings change: FairNVT's Big Nose/Age Acc/DP/EO entries change from 82.1/10.9/1.9 to 83.4/22.9/11.1. The revised objective and search settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance changes. New Table 3 reports Expression/Gender attacker accuracy of 52.1% with one observation versus 92.5% after averaging 50 perturbations. Cross-method attacker scores are removed from image and BIOS benchmark tables; BIOS accuracy/DP and existing supplementary image scores are otherwise retained.

T1.justification: V1 Lemma B.1 incorrectly derives DP=EO=EOpp=0 from unconditional representation independence. V2 Proposition B.1 restricts the conclusion to DP and separately identifies conditional independence given the task label as sufficient for EO/EOpp. Appendix B also adds Proposition B.2 and its factorization proof for idealized independent replacement of the sensitive component. Section 3.2 defines the added HSIC objective mathematically.

C1.justification: The central lightweight noise-based fairness–utility contribution remains. The abstract and contribution bullets shift emphasis from dual-level debiasing and disentanglement toward fair classification supported by empirical leakage reduction. The conclusion qualifies complete disentanglement and the reliability of reusing task embeddings for other downstream tasks.

C2.justification: V2 explains residual sensitive information in the task branch, leakage recovery through averaging, and the interaction between batch size, imbalance and utility. Its conclusion adds substantive limitations concerning sensitive-label availability, stochastic predictions, representation reuse and incomplete disentanglement. Broader-impact discussion also distinguishes benchmark disparities from deployment fairness under distribution shift or unmodeled intersectional groups.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds baseline-specific tuning details for FairVPT, FairViT, FSCL and FairNet and revises the documented search grids. Appendix E newly describes micro-batch gradient accumulation and its limitation for fairness-loss estimation. Architecture dimensions, hardware, parameter counts and runtime disclosures remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Gretton et al. (2005) for HSIC, Liu et al. (2022) for representation-independence evaluation, and Zhou et al. (2025) for FairNet. Appendix A's broader related-work discussion and positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Substantial paragraph rewrites span the abstract, introduction, preliminaries, framework explanations, results narrative and conclusion. Results are reorganized around Pareto trade-offs and representation-specific analysis, noise sensitivity moves into Appendix E, and limitations and broader-impact discussion are added. These changes exceed the accompanying title and publication-header edits.

P2.justification: V2 adds multi-panel Pareto figures, substantially restructures component and attacker tables, and introduces batch-size and inference-variability tables. Saliency grids are rearranged with FairVPT panels removed, benchmark tables lose attacker columns and gain FairNet rows, and the earlier majority-vote diagram disappears. The noise-sensitivity table is relocated to the appendix.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects a central mathematical error in Appendix B and substantially improves assessment of the method through Pareto comparisons, branch-specific leakage tests and explicit failure conditions. These changes make the fairness claims better bounded and supported. Removing comparative attacker scores, the pure-noise control and several uncertainty estimates weakens some evidence, and inconsistencies remain, such as approximately 80% task-embedding attacker accuracy in the prose versus 68.3% in Table 3. Nevertheless, the corrected reasoning and stronger examination of trade-offs and limitations provide a substantial net improvement.
